content:
Apple's iPhone lineup this fall is rumored to be centered around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three most significant feature differences—setting aside price—that could influence your decision to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most apparent, but it's worth mentioning because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic design that iPhones have used for years. The display size and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you're after the traditional iPhone feel, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. Its design is entirely different—the outer display is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner display is similar to an iPad mini.

Cameras: Pro Will Still Hold the Crown

Apple has always packed its most advanced and innovative camera technology into the Pro models. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not include a telephoto lens.

Sources indicate that the iPhone Ultra will still carry the same main, ultrawide, and front cameras as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro models, and is expected to see further improvements this year.

Performance: Both Pack the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Differ

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are both expected to run on the A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will carry forward the aluminum unibody design introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, along with the same vapor chamber cooling. These two changes gave the iPhone 17 Pro better overall performance than its predecessor, as the iPhone can stay cooler during demanding tasks.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a streamlined titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It is also said to potentially feature a vapor chamber, though only one leaker has mentioned this so far. However, due to the different materials, even if the iPhone Ultra shares the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, its performance may fall short under direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
